title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC & Incident Response: Compliance Evidence Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's operational controls and evidence workflows for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident response for security events, compliance evidence collection, and risk & exception handling. It describes responsibilities, configurations, SLOs/thresholds, and step-by-step procedures for preserving and producing evidence for internal and external audits.

Audience
- Security, Engineering, Platform, SRE, Compliance and Legal teams.

Principles and Objectives
- Least privilege by default: roles grant only required capabilities.
- Immutable, tamper-evident audit trails with defined retention and access controls.
- Clear ownership for evidence generation and retention.
- Repeatable, documented workflows for producing audit artifacts.
- Formal risk acceptance and compensating controls when exceptions are required.

1) RBAC & Authentication
- Overview: We use centralized identity via SSO (Okta) with SCIM-managed groups and role mappings to Redwood service roles. Service-to-service authentication uses mTLS and short-lived service tokens issued by the internal token service (tokend).
- Roles and privilege tiers:
  - Platform-Admin: Full console and infra admin (very limited membership; requires 2FA + manager approval).
  - Security-Admin: Access to audit logs, incident tooling, and evidence store.
  - SRE-Operator: Runbooks and operational tooling; restricted infra changes via gated PRs.
  - Developer: Deploy and operate app services; no access to production secrets unless explicitly granted.
  - Auditor (read-only): Read-only view on logs, evidence artifacts, and compliance reports.

- Key controls:
  - All interactive access requires SSO + MFA (Okta + WebAuthn where available).
  - SCIM provisioning: group memberships are the source of truth for role assignment. Changes to SCIM groups must follow change-control (see Change Management section).
  - Privileged access requests: Temporary elevation controlled via the Just-In-Time (JIT) workflow; all JIT sessions are time-bounded, logged, and require an approval ticket.
  - Service accounts: No long-lived keys in code repositories. Service tokens rotate every 1h. Any exception must be recorded in the risk register.

- Ownership:
  - Identity & Access management: Identity team (owner) + Security (review).

2) Audit Logging
- Scope: Capture authentication events, authorization decisions, admin actions, infra changes (Terraform apply), model deployments and config changes, data access events, and selected application-level security events (data export, PII access).

- Logging architecture:
  - Primary ingestion: Fluentd -> centralized secure logging cluster (write-once storage).
  - Storage tiers: Hot (30d) in Elasticsearch for quick lookup, Warm (180d) in object storage with indexing, Cold (3y) archived snapshots for compliance requests (encrypted at rest).
  - Tamper-evidence: WORM-enabled buckets and regular merkle-tree signed catalog of log manifests (SHA256) generated daily by the log-signing job owned by Security.

- Minimum fields to capture (per event): timestamp, actor_id, actor_type (user/service), source_ip, action, resource_id, resource_type, decision (allow/deny), request_payload (redacted), response_status, trace_id, correlation_id.

- SLOs and thresholds:
  - Log delivery: 99.9% of events available in Hot tier within 120s of generation.
  - Signing job success: daily run; 0% failed runs allowed for production; failures generate a P0 alert.

- Access and retention:
  - Access to logs is RBAC-controlled; read-only auditor role exists.
  - Retention policy table (see below).

3) Data Residency & Retention
- Principle: Customer data stored only in approved regions per contract. Backups and replicas follow the same residency boundaries unless explicitly permitted by contract and approved by Legal.

- Retention policy (table):
  | Data Type | Retention (Hot) | Warm/Archive | Owner | Notes |
  |-----------|-----------------|--------------|-------|-------|
  | Authentication & AuthZ logs | 30 days | 3 years (archive) | Security | WORM, hashed manifests |
  | Application telemetry (non-PII) | 90 days | 1 year | Eng-Platform | Aggregate metrics stored longer |
  | PII / Customer-provided dataset snapshots | Per contract (default 7 years) | Encrypted archive | Customer Success & Legal | Delete-on-termination workflow required |
  | Model artifacts (non-customer) | 1 year | 3 years | Eng-Serving-Runtime | Workspace-level metadata retained |
  | Compliance evidence packages | 7 years | 7 years | Security | Immutable evidence store |

- Deletion & disposition:
  - Deletion requests follow the Data Deletion Runbook: verify owner, verify scope, snapshot evidence, perform deletion in all tiers, log deletion events.
  - For customer requests or legal holds, move data to restricted hold bucket; hold owner (Legal) must approve release.

4) Secure SDLC Controls
- Phases & controls:
  - Design: Threat modeling for services that handle sensitive data. Owners: Service owners + Security.
  - Build: Mandatory dependency scanning (Snyk) and secret scanning in CI; static analysis (CodeQL) for all repos flagged high-risk.
  - Review: All production-affecting changes require 2 approvers for infra and 1 approver for app-level PRs; security-critical changes require Security review.
  - Test: CI gated with unit/integration tests, SCA results, and automated policy checks (e.g., no hardcoded secrets, approved base images).
  - Release: Terraform and infra changes applied via a gated pipeline (run by CI bot) with recorded approvals and auditors copied.
  - Post-release: Automated canary telemetry and security health checks for 24-72 hours.

- Evidence produced per release:
  - Signed deploy manifest (including commit SHAs), CI run logs, SCA/scan reports, code review approvals, threat model snapshot (if applicable). These are packaged automatically into the release evidence bundle stored in the evidence store.

5) Incident Response: Security Procedures (High-level)
- Objectives: preserve evidence, contain and remediate, communicate to stakeholders, and perform root cause analysis.

- Triage & severity matrix:
  1. Sev 1 (P0): Active data exfiltration, production denial of service, compromised keys. Response: page on-call SRE & Security, open incident in PagerDuty, immediate containment.
  2. Sev 2 (P1): Suspicious lateral movement, possible data access. Response within 60 minutes.
  3. Sev 3 (P2): Non-production incidents or low-impact security findings. Response within 4 business hours.

- Evidence preservation checklist (initial response):
  1. Freeze relevant hosts (forensic snapshots) or capture memory if compromise suspected.
 2. Take immutable copies of related logs (authentication, application, network flows) and store in evidence bucket (WORM).
 3. Export token/session metadata and revoke tokens where necessary; document the revocation action in the incident timeline.
 4. Maintain chain-of-custody: record who accessed evidence, when, and actions performed.

- Communications:
  - Internal: Incident channel (#incidents/<id>) and secure bridge; status updates every 30 minutes for Sev 1 until resolved.
  - External: Customer notification policy determined by Legal + CS; template messages maintained in the incident playbook.

- Post-incident:
  - 72-hour initial report, 14-day interim report (if ongoing), and a 30-day postmortem with remediation plan and owners.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
- Evidence Store: Centralized, immutable evidence store (GRC Evidence Bucket) with consistent naming and metadata: {control_id}/{evidence_type}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{artifact_id}. All artifacts are checksummed and signed by the evidence service.

- Typical evidence artifacts and generation trigger:
  - RBAC snapshot: daily automated export of role/group memberships and pending JIT approvals (owner: Identity team).
  - Audit log manifests: daily signed manifests (owner: Logging team).
  - Deploy evidence bundle: per-release artifact (owner: Eng-Platform).
  - SDLC scan reports: produced on every PR and archived per release (owner: Dev teams).
  - Incident artifacts: preserved per incident (owner: Incident commander + Security).

- Evidence request procedure (for audits):
  1. Auditor or Compliance opens a ticket in the Evidence Request queue with scope and timeframe.
 2. Evidence owner(s) validate scope and prepare a scoped evidence bundle.
 3. Evidence service produces a signed manifest and delivers evidence bundle to the auditor via a secure temporary access URL or transfers to auditor's agreed storage (per contract).
 4. All evidence deliveries are logged and retained in the evidence audit index.

- SLA for evidence delivery:
  - Internal requests: 3 business days.
  - External accredited auditors: per contract (standard 10 business days); escalations handled by Security/Legal.

7) Risk & Exception Process
- When a control cannot be implemented as required, teams must submit an Exception Request that includes: description, impacted control, business justification, estimated exposure, compensating controls, and expiration date.

- Review & approval flow:
  1. Submit request to Risk Register (Confluence form).
 2. Initial security review within 5 business days.
 3. If acceptable, Security + Risk Committee approve with assigned mitigations and monitoring. High-risk exceptions require CISO and Legal signoff.
  4. Exception record in the Risk Register with owner and expiry.

- Monitoring & revalidation:
  - Exceptions are revalidated at least quarterly or on major infra changes. Automated monitoring metrics (where applicable) are required as compensating controls (example: elevated logging, IP allowlists, reduced token TTLs).

Appendices
A. Key Commands & Scripts
- Log signing check: 
  curl -sS https://evidence.redwood.corp/log-signing/status | jq
- RBAC export (identity team):
  ./scripts/export-rbac --output rbac-snapshot-$(date +%F).json --groups scim:prod-access
- Evidence bundle generation (release):
  ci/tools/generate_evidence_bundle --release $RELEASE_TAG --out /evidence/$RELEASE_TAG.tar.gz

- AUTHZ_LOGS: hot=30d,warm=3y,cold=7y
- APP_TELEMETRY: hot=90d,warm=1y,cold=3y
- PII_DATASETS: hot=per-contract,warm=per-contract,cold=per-contract
- RELEASE_EVIDENCE: hot=7y,warm=7y,cold=7y

E. Review cadence
- This document: annual review (Security owner) and after any major control change. Evidence workflows and retention schedules reviewed quarterly by Security + Legal.

F. FAQ (selected)
- Q: How do I request temporary production access?
  A: Create a JIT access request in the Identity portal and provide justification and duration. All requests generate an approval ticket.

- Q: Who can produce logs for an auditor?
  A: Authorized members of the Logging team or Security with Auditor role; requests route through the Evidence Request queue.
